supplement.where: Supplementary Information B and Tables S1 and S2 are cited in the text (p. 7-8, p. 19); no URL is given and the PDF ends with the references on p. 34
supplement.holds: Supplementary Information B is cited for all human instructions and AI prompts (pp. 7-8, section 2.1.3). Table S1 is cited for descriptive statistics for all Experiment 1 metrics (p. 8, section 2.1.4). Tables S1 and S2 are cited for Experiment 6 selection strategies and fitness ratings (p. 19, section 3.2.4). The supplement is absent from the available PDF; exact arm means and SDs in that supplement have not been verified.

paper_design_summary: Eight experiments compare output from GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4o (and GPT-4-turbo for image tasks), called through the OpenAI API with the human instructions, with output from 60 to 100 Chinese human participants per experiment who worked without AI. Study 1 scores creative tasks: Alternate Uses Task (novelty, appropriateness, flexibility by raters), Remote Associates Test and insight-problem accuracy, and two writing tasks (five-sentence stories and advertising stories rated for novelty and appropriateness or effectiveness, plus cosine-similarity homogeneity). Study 2 compares process measures (association semantic distance and forward flow, representational change accuracy, creative evaluation weights, creative selection decision error); no participant received AI assistance, and Experiment 1 is described as preregistered on OSF (p. 6).

studies.label: Experiment 1 (Alternate Uses Task, humans vs GPT models)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned to AI assistance. Human AUT responses and independently generated model responses were compared between source groups, with model response counts matched to human counts. Randomization concerned which object was presented per trial.
assignment.quote: After human data collection, we used a Python script to call the OpenAI API, gathering responses from GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, and GPT-4 for the AUT.
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 6, section 2.1.1: OSF preregistration stated; no registration URL or identifier is supplied.

outcomes.name: AUT novelty rating (human vs each GPT model)
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.treatment_arm: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4o output (each compared with humans; 100 instances per model)
contrasts.reported: GPT-3.5-turbo (t= 5.32, 95% CI = [-0.54, -0.19], p < 0.001), GPT-4 (t= 5.10, 95% CI = [-0.51, -0.16], p < 0.001), and GPT-4o (t= 8.89, 95% CI = [-0.76, -0.42], , p < 0.001) all got significantly higher novelty scores than humans. Figure 1A displays group results; Table S1 is cited for descriptive statistics, but exact arm means and SDs in the unavailable supplement have not been verified.

eligibility.reason: All eight experiments compare independently generated model responses with human responses; no people were assigned to AI assistance (pp. 6-24, each experiment's participant and procedure sections). Recruitment/data-collection totals exceed the threshold, but separate analyzed-people counts are not reported (pp. 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20, 22, participant sections); Experiment 4 reports two withdrawals without task-specific human analysis counts (p. 12, section 2.4.1). Creativity ratings and story homogeneity are scored on output (p. 7, section 2.1.2; p. 13, section 2.4.2). The paper therefore remains AI-versus-human context and is not core evidence.

one_line_finding: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, and GPT-4o produced Alternate Uses ideas rated more novel than 100 humans' ideas (t = 5.32, 5.10, 8.89, all p < 0.001; p. 8), but their five-sentence and advertising stories were rated less novel (human-minus-AI 95% CIs from [0.10, 0.57] to [0.24, 0.84]) and were more homogeneous in cosine similarity (t from -9.14 to -22.34, all p < 0.001) than stories by about 61 to 63 humans (pp. 13-14, Figure 4).
